items.title: CVE-2026-71394 - GNU Emacs for Android improperly validates the table header input in sfnt_read_t...
items.body:
GNU Emacs for Android improperly validates the table header input in sfnt_read_table_directory() in src/sfnt.c. Due to an incorrect comparison variable in the read-length check, a crafted font file that claims to contain more table directory entries than actually present causes the parser to return a struct with uninitialized heap memory in the table directory entries. An attacker can deliver a malicious font file via email, EWW (Emacs Web Wowser), or documents with custom faces, causing Emacs to load it. This leads to the use of uninitialized heap data in subsequent table lookups, potentially resulting in information disclosure, crashes, or arbitrary memory access on 32-bit targets.


This issue is fixed after commit 7621ee1d01229d50e5c0cddea6bf0b01095a62cf

items.title: CVE-2026-71393 - GNU Emacs for Android is vulnerable to an integer overflow in sfnt_read_name_tab...
items.body:
GNU Emacs for Android is vulnerable to an integer overflow in sfnt_read_name_table() in src/sfnt.c. The function computes an allocation size using a 32-bit length value from a TrueType font file without overflow checking. On 32-bit targets, a crafted font causes the calculation to wrap, resulting in an undersized heap allocation. A subsequent read() call writes beyond the buffer, causing a heap buffer overflow. items.title: CVE-2026-66484 - GNU cpio contains a Path Traversal vulnerability in its tar archive extraction f...
items.body:

When extracting a tar archive in copy-in mode with the --no-absolute-filenames option, the extracted file name is normalized but the tar hard-link target is passed to the link_to_name function without equivalent sanitization before calling link function. A tar archive provided by an attacker, containing a hard-link entry whose linkname is set to an absolute path outside the extraction directory, can cause cpio to create a hard link to an existing file outside the intended extraction directory, breaking the expected guarantee of --no-absolute-filenames and allowing archive-controlled linkage to external files.

items.body: A vulnerability in keras-team/keras versions <= 3.15.0 allows for a denial of service (DoS) attack when loading malicious .keras model files via the keras.models.load_model() function. The H5IOStore.__getitem__ method in keras/src/saving/saving_lib.py does not validate the shape or size of datasets, leading to unbounded memory allocation. A specially crafted .keras file can exploit this flaw to trigger an out-of-memory (OOM) condition, causing the process to be terminated (exit code 137). items.title: Zephyr ProjectのZephyrにおける不正な認証に関する脆弱性
items.body: ZephyrのBluetoothホストは、GATTキャラクタリスティックを2つの連続した属性として宣言しています。1つはパーミッションがBT_GATT_PERM_READにハードコーディングされたCharacteristic Declaration（キャラクタリスティック宣言）であり、もう1つはアプリケーションが指定したセキュリティパーミッション（例えばBT_GATT_PERM_READ_ENCRYPT / READ_AUTHEN / READ_LESC）を持つCharacteristic Value属性です。パブリックのnotifyおよびindicate APIは明示的にどちらの属性も受け入れており、宣言属性を渡すことがドキュメントに記載された一般的な慣習となっています。各通知または通知指示の送信前に、ホストはgatt_notify()、gatt_indicate()、およびgatt_notify_multiple_verify_params()（subsys/bluetooth/host/gatt.c）内でbt_gatt_check_perm()を用いてparams-＞attrに対しリンクのセキュリティを再チェックしています。アプリケーションがCharacteristic Declaration属性を渡した場合、ホストは値ハンドルを正しくリダイレクトしましたが、params-＞attrは宣言属性を指したままであったため、セキュリティチェックは宣言のパーミッション（セキュリティ不要）を評価し、値のパーミッションを評価しませんでした。その結果、キャラクタリスティック値に設定された暗号化／認証／LESCの要件がスキップされてしまいました。Notify-Multipleの経路ではさらにLE Secure Connections要件を省略したマスクが使用されていました。リモートのピアは、（ペアリングや暗号化なしでも）接続後にClient Characteristic Configurationディスクリプタを書き込み通知または指示を有効にすることで、この情報漏洩を引き起こします。これにより、要求されるセキュリティレベルに達していないリンク上で保護された値をサーバが送出してしまいます。影響は、アプリケーションが暗号化／認証が必要なnotify/indicateキャラクタリスティックを宣言し、かつCCCがより低いセキュリティレベルで書き込み可能な場合に限り、情報漏洩やアクセス制御の回避が発生します。メモリ安全性や可用性に対する影響はありません。修正では、許可チェック前に宣言属性を次の値属性にマッピングするbt_gatt_attr_resolve_value()を追加し、Notify-Multipleの経路ではBT_GATT_PERM_READ_ENCRYPT_MASKの全てを使用してLESC要件も強制するよう変更しています。

items.title: CVE-2026-12372 - A Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability exists in nltk/nltk versions ...
items.body: A Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability exists in nltk/nltk versions 3.9.4 and the current develop branch. The `nltk.pathsec.validate_network_url()` function, intended to prevent SSRF by rejecting internal network addresses, fails to reject IPs in the RFC 6598 shared address space (`100.64.0.0/10`). This occurs because Python's `ipaddress` module does not classify such addresses as `is_private` or `is_global`, and the current guard only checks `is_private` and a few explicit categories. An attacker who can influence a URL passed to NLTK's network-loading helpers can exploit this vulnerability to make a strict-mode application send requests to shared-address-space hosts, potentially exposing non-public infrastructure reachable from the application host. The impact is limited to SSRF-style confidentiality exposure, with no code execution claimed.

items.title: CVE-2026-70395 - Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic vulnerability in...
items.body:
Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic vulnerability in ash-project ash allows an attacker to forge a relationship to a record they cannot name, and to recover the secret value used to look it up.

When manage_relationship is used with on_lookup: :relate on a belongs_to relationship, the client-supplied lookup value is passed to Ash.Query.filter/2 without being cast to the attribute type. A nested map submitted where a scalar is expected is therefore interpreted as a filter predicate rather than a literal, so a lookup for a specific record becomes a query for any record matching a condition. The same path omits Ash.Query.limit(1), leaving Ash.read_one/2 able to distinguish no match from one match from several, which turns comparison predicates into an oracle for the lookup value. Authorization is unaffected; the destination read policy still applies.

This issue affects ash: from 1.52.0-rc.11 before 3.31.1.

items.title: CVE-2026-69659 - Uncontrolled Resource Consumption vulnerability in ash-project ash allows an att...
items.body:
Uncontrolled Resource Consumption vulnerability in ash-project ash allows an attacker to exhaust the memory of the node via a crafted keyset pagination cursor.

Read actions with keyset pagination deserialize the client-supplied page[:after] or page[:before] cursor in decode_values/2 in lib/ash/page/keyset.ex, which base64-decodes the value and passes it to :erlang.binary_to_term/2 without bounding its size. The Erlang external term format supports zlib-compressed payloads, which the decoder inflates transparently, so a cursor of a few kilobytes can allocate tens of megabytes of heap in a single call. Ash itself only ever encodes cursors uncompressed, so the decoder accepts a term shape its encoder never produces. Concurrent requests aggregate these allocations and can terminate the node.

This issue affects ash: from 1.17.0 before 3.31.1.

items.title: CVE-2026-15534 - Perl versions through 5.45.1 have out-of-bounds heap reads and writes during reg...
items.body:
Perl versions through 5.45.1 have out-of-bounds heap reads and writes during regular expression matching via an undersized superlinear cache in S_regmatch.

The regex engine's superlinear cache holds one bit per subject position for each participating WHILEM node, so the bit count is the subject length plus one times the number of nodes. Nothing checks that product for positive overflow of the signed 32-bit count: a 286331153 byte subject matched against a pattern with 15 participating nodes stores the count as 14, leaving a two byte cache. The cache is then indexed from the real match position and node number, so reads go past the end of the allocation, and on failure CACHEsayNO sets a bit past it.

A caller that matches an attacker controlled subject of this size against a pattern of this shape can crash the process or corrupt heap memory.
